topic: How four-wheel steering turns a giant car like a compact

layout.title: How Four-Wheel Steering Turns a Giant Car Like a Compact

shows.does: the giant truck turns its front wheels and swings through a wide arc
the long tail swings out and knocks an orange post flat with a crash
a yellow rod appears on the rear axle, the rear wheels turn against the front and the truck pivots tight; the post stands back up
a glowing outline traces the truck
at speed the turned rear wheels whip the tail round hard
a blue computer box appears and sends a signal; the rear wheels swing to turn the same way as the front and the tail straightens
the rear wheels fall back straight and sit there
an orange electric motor appears by the rod and the rear wheels turn again
the rod snaps in two and the whole truck veers off line
a green spring appears on the rod, the rear wheels pull straight and the truck straightens
the rear wheels turn too far and sparks fly where they scrape the body
the rear wheels come back to a small angle and the sparks stop
night falls; the truck sits in its turn while its headlights shine straight ahead, past the dark curve
the headlights swivel into the turn
rain falls and the tail skids out
one rear wheel glows as it brakes and the tail swings back in line
the truck swings wide again past where it should park
all four wheels turn the same way and the truck slides sideways
the rear wheels swing back straight, hidden under the long body far from the cab
a screen on a post counts the rear wheel angle up to 10
the truck slides back toward the post
side mirrors appear on the cab and daylight comes back
the front wheels steer, the rear wheels turn against them and the truck pivots tight round the standing post
the finished truck beside the post

layout.why: A long flatbed truck on an open road, seen from a little above so every wheel's angle reads, with an orange post at the corner. Its trip (corner, highway, rear axle, wheel wells, night road, wet road, parking spot, reversing) brings one problem after another: a rod, a computer, a motor, a spring, a 10 degree limit, swivelling headlights, one-wheel braking, crab-walk parking, an angle screen and mirrors. At the end it pivots tight round the same post it flattened at the start. High shots on the axles for each wheel change, the whole truck for each swing.

sentences.text: If you steer only the front wheels, you have a wide turn.
But its long tail swings out and flattens a post.
So you link a rod that turns the rear wheels.
This is four-wheel steering.
But on the highway, the turned rear wheels whip the tail.
So a computer turns them the same way above 37 miles per hour.
But now its tiny signal cannot shove the wheels; they sit.
So an electric motor pushes the rod.
But if the motor fails, the rod snaps; it veers.
So a spring pulls the rear wheels straight.
But turned too far, the rear wheels scrape the body.
So you limit them to about 10 degrees.
But at night, 10 degrees of turn leaves the curve dark.
So the headlights swivel into the turn.
But in rain, the swiveling lights show the tail skidding.
So the computer brakes one rear wheel to straighten it.
But parking, the braked giant swings wide of the spot.
So at a crawl, all four wheels turn alike, and it slides diagonally.
But sliding diagonally, the rear wheels turn unseen.
So a screen shows the driver the rear wheel angle.
But reversing by screen alone, the tail rolls toward the post.
So you add mirrors that show the tail.
Steer the front wheels, and it circles the post like a compact.
Congratulations, you built a giant that turns tight.
